1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""Baseline heuristic router (starter idea 01) + cache-aware cost report.
3	
4	Policy: short-prompt calls early in a trajectory go to a cheaper sibling model;
5	everything else stays on the logged model. Deliberately simple — an honest floor.
6	
7	Usage: python scripts/baseline_router.py export/   -> writes results/routes.jsonl
8	"""
9	import json, sys
10	from pathlib import Path
11	from load_trajectories import iter_requests, group_trajectories, est_tokens
12	from cost_model import trajectory_cost, logged_route, load_pricing
13	
14	# Cheaper sibling per family. Anonymized ids: within claude, sonnet is assumed the
15	# mid tier and fable the small tier; the gpt-5.6 variants (sol/terra/luna) have no
16	# published tier order. ASSUMPTION — check the reconstructed traces (e.g. which model
17	# gets long-context work) before trusting it.
18	CHEAP = {"claude": "claude-fable-5", "gpt": "gpt-5.6-sol"}
19	
20	def cheap_for(model):
21	    return CHEAP["claude"] if model.startswith("claude") else CHEAP["gpt"]
22	
23	SMALL_TRAJECTORY = 15_000  # est. input tokens; ~40% of real trajectories fall under this
24	
25	def route_trajectory(calls):
26	    """Baseline route: send WHOLE small trajectories to the cheap sibling, keep the rest
27	    on the logged model. Whole-trajectory routing respects the one-model-per-trajectory
28	    premise and never pays the cache-reset penalty for a mid-task switch."""
29	    total = sum(est_tokens(c["input"]) for c in calls)
30	    if total < SMALL_TRAJECTORY:
31	        return [cheap_for(c["model"]) for c in calls]
32	    return [c["model"] for c in calls]
33	
34	def main():
35	    export = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "export"
36	    pricing = load_pricing()
37	    groups = group_trajectories(r for _, _, r in iter_requests(export))
38	    Path("results").mkdir(exist_ok=True)
39	    out = open("results/routes.jsonl", "w")
40	    tot_logged = tot_routed = 0.0
41	    for key, calls in groups.items():
42	        logged = logged_route(calls); routed = route_trajectory(calls)
43	        c_logged, _ = trajectory_cost(calls, logged, pricing)
44	        c_routed, _ = trajectory_cost(calls, routed, pricing)
45	        tot_logged += c_logged; tot_routed += c_routed
46	        out.write(json.dumps({"trajectory": key, "n_calls": len(calls), "logged_model": logged[0],
47	                              "route": routed, "cost_logged_usd": round(c_logged, 6),
48	                              "cost_routed_usd": round(c_routed, 6),
49	                              "switches": sum(1 for i in range(1, len(routed)) if routed[i] != routed[i-1])}) + "\n")
50	    out.close()
51	    print(f"logged cost (est. input tokens, assumed prices):  ${tot_logged:,.4f}")
52	    print(f"routed cost:  ${tot_routed:,.4f}  ({(tot_routed/tot_logged-1):+.1%}, cache-aware)")
53	    print("NOTE: no outputs/usage in the export — token counts are estimates, output cost excluded,")
54	    print("and this baseline has NO outcome estimate. Constructing one is the challenge.")
55	    print("wrote results/routes.jsonl")
56	
57	if __name__ == "__main__": main()
58

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""Cache-aware cost model on ESTIMATED tokens.
3	
4	The export has no `usage` field: every token count here is estimated as
5	serialized chars / 4 (see load_trajectories.est_tokens). The cache trap still
6	applies: providers cache the shared input prefix across consecutive calls of a
7	task, and a model switch resets that cache — the first call after a switch
8	pays the uncached rate for the whole prefix.
9	
10	Cached share of call i is estimated as the token size of the item-level prefix
11	that call i shares with call i-1 of the same trajectory.
12	
13	Model ids in the export are anonymized (families claude-opus/-sonnet/-fable and
14	gpt-5.6-* across generations, e.g. claude-opus-5, claude-opus-4-8, gpt-5.6-terra),
15	so no public price sheet exists. DEFAULT_PRICING is an ASSUMPTION for relative
16	comparisons; unknown ids fall back to their family rate by prefix match — if a price sheet is posted in the
17	challenge Discord, put it in scripts/pricing.json; either way, state your
18	pricing assumption in the writeup.
19	"""
20	import json
21	from pathlib import Path
22	from load_trajectories import est_tokens
23	
24	DEFAULT_PRICING = {  # per 1M est. tokens: [uncached_input, cached_input, output] — ASSUMED, not official
25	    "claude-opus": [15.00, 1.50, 75.00],   # family prefixes: match any generation (claude-opus-5, claude-opus-4-8, ...)
26	    "claude-sonnet": [3.00, 0.30, 15.00],
27	    "claude-fable": [0.80, 0.08, 4.00],
28	    "gpt-5.6": [2.00, 0.50, 8.00],
29	    "_default": [2.00, 0.40, 8.00],
30	}
31	
32	def load_pricing():
33	    p = Path(__file__).parent / "pricing.json"
34	    return json.loads(p.read_text()) if p.exists() else DEFAULT_PRICING
35	
36	def price_of(model, pricing):
37	    if model in pricing: return pricing[model]
38	    for prefix in sorted(pricing, key=len, reverse=True):  # longest family prefix wins
39	        if prefix != "_default" and model.startswith(prefix): return pricing[prefix]
40	    return pricing["_default"]
41	
42	def shared_prefix_tokens(prev_req, req):
43	    """Estimated tokens of the item-level input prefix shared with the previous call."""
44	    shared = 0
45	    for a, b in zip(prev_req["input"], req["input"]):
46	        if a == b: shared += est_tokens(a)
47	        else: break
48	    return shared
49	
50	def trajectory_cost(calls, route, pricing=None):
51	    """Cost of a reconstructed trajectory (calls ordered by input length) if call i
52	    had been served by route[i]. Cache-aware: the shared prefix is billed at the
53	    cached rate only when route[i] == route[i-1]. Output tokens are unknowable
54	    (no outputs in the export) and are NOT included — say so when you quote numbers.
55	    Returns (usd, uncached_input_tokens_est)."""
56	    pricing = pricing or load_pricing()
57	    usd, uncached_total = 0.0, 0
58	    for i, c in enumerate(calls):
59	        inp = est_tokens(c["input"])
60	        cached = shared_prefix_tokens(calls[i - 1], c) if (i > 0 and route[i] == route[i - 1]) else 0
61	        cached = min(cached, inp)
62	        uncached = inp - cached
63	        pu, pc, _ = price_of(route[i], pricing)
64	        usd += (uncached * pu + cached * pc) / 1e6
65	        uncached_total += uncached
66	    return usd, uncached_total
67	
68	def logged_route(calls): return [c["model"] for c in calls]
69

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""Load a redacted-trajectories export and reconstruct trajectories.
3	
4	The export is chunked JSONL — `trajectories_v1_<index>.jsonl.tar.gz` archives that
5	extract to `export/trajectories_v1_<index>.jsonl` (any `export/*.jsonl` is read). Each line is one LLM
6	request: `model`, `input` (Responses-format item list), `tools`. There are no
7	trajectory ids — requests of the same task are recovered by grouping on the
8	task's opening messages (system + first user text), then ordering by history
9	length (each request's input contains every item of the previous one).
10	
11	Usage: python scripts/load_trajectories.py export/
12	Importable: iter_requests, group_trajectories, est_tokens, first_user_text.
13	"""
14	import json, sys, hashlib
15	from pathlib import Path
16	from collections import Counter, defaultdict
17	
18	def iter_requests(export_dir):
19	    """Yield (chunk_name, line_no, request) for every line of every chunk."""
20	    chunks = sorted(Path(export_dir).glob("*.jsonl"))
21	    if not chunks:
22	        sys.exit(f"no *.jsonl chunks found in {export_dir}")
23	    for p in chunks:
24	        with open(p) as f:
25	            for i, line in enumerate(f):
26	                if line.strip():
27	                    yield p.name, i, json.loads(line)
28	
29	def first_user_text(req):
30	    """Text of the first user message — stable across all requests of a task."""
31	    for item in req["input"]:
32	        if item.get("role") == "user":
33	            c = item.get("content")
34	            if isinstance(c, str): return c
35	            return " ".join(p.get("text", "") for p in c if p.get("type") == "input_text")
36	    return ""
37	
38	def group_key(req):
39	    return hashlib.sha1(first_user_text(req)[:2000].encode()).hexdigest()[:16]
40	
41	def group_trajectories(requests):
42	    """Group requests by task and order each group by input length (= call order)."""
43	    groups = defaultdict(list)
44	    for req in requests: groups[group_key(req)].append(req)
45	    for k in groups: groups[k].sort(key=lambda r: len(r["input"]))
46	    return dict(groups)
47	
48	def est_tokens(obj):
49	    """Crude token estimate: serialized chars / 4. There is NO usage field in the
50	    export — every token number in this repo is an estimate. State that in your writeup."""
51	    return len(json.dumps(obj)) // 4 if not isinstance(obj, str) else len(obj) // 4
52	
53	def main():
54	    export = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "export"
55	    reqs = [r for _, _, r in iter_requests(export)]
56	    models = Counter(r["model"] for r in reqs)
57	    print(f"requests={len(reqs)}  per-model request counts: {dict(models)}")
58	    groups = group_trajectories(reqs)
59	    sizes = sorted(len(v) for v in groups.values())
60	    print(f"reconstructed trajectories={len(groups)}  calls/trajectory min/median/max: "
61	          f"{sizes[0]}/{sizes[len(sizes)//2]}/{sizes[-1]}")
62	    mixed = [k for k, v in groups.items() if len({r['model'] for r in v}) > 1]
63	    print(f"trajectories with >1 model: {len(mixed)}"
64	          + ("  (premise says one model per trajectory — inspect these)" if mixed else "  (matches the one-model-per-trajectory premise)"))
65	    total = sum(est_tokens(r["input"]) for r in reqs)
66	    print(f"est. input tokens (chars/4, no usage in export): {total:,}")
67	    # spot-check one request for the expected fields
68	    r = reqs[0]
69	    missing = [k for k in ("model", "input", "tools") if k not in r]
70	    extra = [k for k in r if k not in ("model", "input", "tools")]
71	    print(f"schema check on first request: missing={missing or 'none'} extra={extra or 'none'}")
72	
73	if __name__ == "__main__": main()
74

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""Cost–quality frontier from results/routes.jsonl.
3	
4	Quality here is a PLACEHOLDER (fraction of calls kept on the logged model) so the
5	pipeline runs end to end. Replace `quality()` with your constructed outcome signal —
6	that replacement is the actual challenge.
7	
8	Usage: python scripts/plot_frontier.py results/routes.jsonl
9	Writes results/frontier.csv (+ frontier.png if matplotlib is installed).
10	"""
11	import json, sys, csv
12	from pathlib import Path
13	
14	def quality(rec):  # PLACEHOLDER — replace with your outcome signal
15	    kept = sum(1 for i, m in enumerate(rec["route"]) if m == rec["logged_model"])
16	    return kept / len(rec["route"])
17	
18	def main():
19	    src = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "results/routes.jsonl"
20	    recs = [json.loads(l) for l in open(src)]
21	    total_calls = sum(r["n_calls"] for r in recs)
22	    # Sweep how much of the router's proposal to adopt: adopt for the cheapest X% of
23	    # trajectories first (they are the safest bets), keep the rest on the logged model.
24	    by_size = sorted(recs, key=lambda r: r["cost_logged_usd"])
25	    rows = []
26	    for frac in [i / 10 for i in range(0, 11)]:
27	        adopt = set(id(r) for r in by_size[: int(round(frac * len(recs)))])
28	        cost = sum(r["cost_routed_usd"] if id(r) in adopt else r["cost_logged_usd"] for r in recs)
29	        kept = sum((quality(r) if id(r) in adopt else 1.0) * r["n_calls"] for r in recs)
30	        rows.append({"adopt_frac": frac, "cost_usd": round(cost, 4),
31	                     "quality_placeholder": round(kept / total_calls, 3)})
32	    out = Path(src).parent / "frontier.csv"
33	    with open(out, "w", newline="") as f:
34	        w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=rows[0].keys()); w.writeheader(); w.writerows(rows)
35	    print(f"wrote {out}")
36	    for r in rows: print(r)
37	    try:
38	        import matplotlib
39	        matplotlib.use("Agg")
40	        import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
41	        plt.figure(figsize=(6, 4))
42	        plt.plot([r["cost_usd"] for r in rows], [r["quality_placeholder"] for r in rows], "o-", color="#6748FD")
43	        plt.xlabel("cost (USD, estimated tokens, cache-aware)"); plt.ylabel("quality (placeholder)")
44	        plt.title("Cost–quality frontier"); plt.tight_layout()
45	        png = Path(src).parent / "frontier.png"; plt.savefig(png, dpi=150)
46	        print(f"wrote {png}")
47	    except ImportError:
48	        print("matplotlib not installed — skipped PNG (CSV is enough)")
49	
50	if __name__ == "__main__": main()

# Model Router — Viktor Challenge Summary

## Title & Event
"Model Router — Viktor challenge" is a hackathon competition hosted by TUM.ai in Munich (August 22–23, 2026) where participants build intelligent routing systems for LLM calls.

## Problem Statement
Viktor is an AI employee that operates in Slack and Microsoft Teams, executing tasks through sequences of LLM calls. The core challenge addresses an "open off-policy problem": given real execution traces where a single model served an entire trajectory, determine which model should have handled each individual call to optimize cost, quality, or a custom trade-off.

## Dataset & Approach
Participants receive "static offline export of real Viktor trajectories" in OpenAI-compatible format. Each line contains three fields: model identifier, full input history, and available tools. Notably, the dataset excludes output, usage data, and trajectory IDs—forcing participants to reconstruct outcomes and estimate token consumption themselves.

## Key Methodological Challenge
The central twist involves cache dynamics: when a routing decision switches models mid-trajectory, it resets the inference cache, creating a secondary cost factor. Participants must estimate this effect while acknowledging the log only reveals what actually occurred, requiring off-policy evaluation techniques.

## Evaluation Criteria
Solutions are judged on three dimensions:

1. **Routing Insight**: Demonstrable structure in routing decisions, not black-box optimization
2. **Evaluation Rigor**: Honest methodology acknowledging failure modes and estimation limitations
3. **Presentation Clarity**: Defendable cost-quality frontiers with transparent weakness acknowledgment

## Deliverables
Teams submit: a router policy, a defended evaluation methodology, and a five-minute presentation showing the cost-quality frontier their system achieves versus baselines and random routing.

## Special Considerations
- No GPU or API keys required; baselines train on laptops in minutes
- A special prize targets superior off-policy evaluation insights
- Teams retain portfolio pieces; data redistribution is prohibited

No `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` exist yet (referenced by the setup skill but not present). I have enough to summarize.

## What this codebase is

This is a **TUM.ai hackathon submission** (Aug 22–23, 2026) for the **"Model Router — Viktor Challenge."** Viktor is an AI employee (operates in Slack/Teams) whose real execution traces — sequences of LLM calls per task — were logged with a single model serving the whole trajectory. The challenge: build a **router** that decides, retroactively/off-policy, which model *should* have handled each individual call to optimize a cost–quality trade-off, then defend the methodology.

The dataset itself (`trajectories_v1_01.jsonl.tar.gz`, ~30MB) is present locally but excluded from git. Each line is one LLM request with only `model`, `input` (full message history so far), and `tools` — deliberately **no `output` and no `usage`/token counts**, and no trajectory IDs, forcing participants to reconstruct trajectories and estimate everything themselves. Models are anonymized into families (`claude-opus/-sonnet/-fable`, `gpt-5.6-sol/terra/luna`, across generations).

## Repo layout

- **`scripts/`** — the working pipeline (stdlib Python, no GPU/API keys needed):
  - `load_trajectories.py` — reads chunked JSONL, regroups requests into trajectories by hashing each task's first user message, orders calls by input length (proxy for call order), and does a crude token estimate (`chars/4`).
  - `cost_model.py` — cache-aware pricing model: bills the *shared input prefix* between consecutive same-model calls at a cached rate, and treats a mid-trajectory model switch as a cache-reset (full uncached price). Pricing (`DEFAULT_PRICING`) is an explicit **assumption**, not a real price sheet.
  - `baseline_router.py` — the "honest floor" baseline: routes whole small trajectories (<15k est. tokens) to a cheaper sibling model (`sonnet→fable`, `gpt-5.6-*→sol`), leaves everything else on the logged model. Outputs `results/routes.jsonl`.
  - `plot_frontier.py` — sweeps how much of the router's proposal to adopt (cheapest trajectories first) and produces a cost vs. quality frontier (`results/frontier.csv` + `.png`). **Quality is currently a placeholder** (fraction of calls kept on the logged model) — replacing it with a real constructed outcome signal is flagged as "the actual challenge."
  - `make_synthetic_sample.py` — generates a schema-identical synthetic `export/` for pipeline development before/without the real dataset.

- **`results/`** — baseline run outputs: `routes.jsonl` (953 trajectories), `frontier.csv`, `frontier.png`. Current baseline shows logged cost ≈$146 → routed cost ≈$113–146 depending on adoption fraction, with the placeholder "quality" dropping from 1.0 to 0.64 at full adoption.

- **`skills/`** (Claude Code slash-command skills authored for this challenge):
  - `/setup` — environment/dataset setup, sanity checks, run the first baseline.
  - `/make-presentation` — builds the 5-minute judged defense deck from `templates/presentation.html`, fixed slide order (Title → Objective → Signal → Frontier chart → Honesty/failure modes → Ask/close), Viktor brand colors (`#6748FD` violet / `#150079` navy / `#FFBD9E` peach).
  - `/prepare-submission` — packages `submission/` (manifest, code, results, presentation) into a zip, explicitly forbidding inclusion of the raw dataset.

- **`templates/presentation.html`** — the branded, self-contained (no network) slide deck template with `<!-- FILL -->` slots, arrow-key/fullscreen navigation.

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field


class LLMModel(BaseModel):
    """Describes a single LLM model/variant and everything needed to price and compare it."""

    name: str
    family: str
    tier: int = Field(description="Relative capability/cost tier within its family; lower = cheaper/smaller.")

    cache_window_size: int = Field(description="Max number of tokens that can be served from cache (e.g. context window eligible for prompt caching).")

    input_price_per_1m: float = Field(description="USD per 1M uncached input tokens.")
    cached_input_price_per_1m: float = Field(description="USD per 1M cached input tokens.")
    output_price_per_1m: float = Field(description="USD per 1M uncached output tokens.")
    cached_output_price_per_1m: float = Field(description="USD per 1M cached output tokens.")
